span: Section 197 of the CrPC would not apply to a case if a public servant is accused of any offence which is de hors or not connected to the discharge of his or her official duty
why: Court states previous sanction is required for acts in discharge of official duty but s.197 does not apply to offences unconnected with that duty.

span: protection of sub-section (1) of Section 197 of CrPC is available only to such public servants whose appointing authority is the Central Government or the State Government and not to every public servant
why: Court says sanction under s.197 is required for such public servants but the protection is not available to every public servant.

span: Whether on account of s.19(1), the scope of inquiry u/ s. 156(3) Cr.P.C. can be said to be one of taking ‘cognizance’ thereby requiring the prior sanction in case of a public servant
why: Headnote frames whether sanction is needed even at the s.156(3) investigation stage and refers the question to a larger bench; no answer is given.

span: Whether sanction u/s. 197 Cr.P.C. is required to prosecute respondent No. 2 who faces accusation amongst others of creating fake documents by misusing his official position as a Village Accountant
why: Issue statement and the High Court's view; the court's own holding begins at the end of the passage and is in the next passage.

span: Sanction of the Government, to prosecute a police officer, for any act related to the discharge of an official duty, is imperative to protect the police officer
why: Headnote holding: sanction is a legal requirement for prosecuting a police officer for acts connected with official duty (s.197 CrPC); not every offence attracts it.

span: It is only when there is a direct and reasonable nexus between the nature of the duties cast upon the public servant and the act constituting an offence that the protection under Section 197 CrPC may be available and not otherwise.
why: Quoted from Urmila Devi and said only to 'have some relevance' to a s.199(4) question; adoption on the s.197 point is not stated.
